- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true values often spike higher in the middle to late period, suggesting model fails to capture sudden demand or policy-driven surges.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., 90+), model forecasts remain flat or slightly increasing, missing the peak and failing to anticipate subsequent mean reversion or stabilization.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward lower values, particularly when recent history includes high prices — it underreacts to recent highs.
- Forecasts appear to lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model does not adequately adjust for mean reversion after sustained high prices — it overestimates continuation of upward trend.
- When true values show a sharp drop or correction, model forecasts remain stubbornly high, indicating poor sensitivity to reversal signals.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price spikes, especially when preceded by a low or volatile recent period.
